instruction:
Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements run-length encoding and decoding. 
Run-length encoding is a data compression technique that replaces repetitive patterns of data with a single data value and a count of how many times that value is repeated.
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs for the encoding operation:

Inputs: a set of n input data values (in1, in2, ..., inn)
Outputs: a set of m encoded data values (out1, out2, ..., outm)
The module should also have the following parameters:

n: the number of input data values
m: the number of encoded data values
w: the number of bits per data value
Your module should implement the following functionality for the encoding operation:

The circuit should count the number of consecutive occurrences of each input data value.
The circuit should output an encoded data value and a count for each input data value that is repeated consecutively.
To implement the run-length encoding, you should use Verilog code to compare each input data value with the previous input data value. 
You should then count the number of consecutive occurrences of each data value and output an encoded data value and a count for each repetition.

For the decoding operation, your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a set of m encoded data values (in1, in2, ..., inm)
Outputs: a set of n decoded data values (out1, out2, ..., outn)
The module should also have the following parameters:

n: the number of decoded data values
m: the number of encoded data values
w: the number of bits per data value
Your module should implement the following functionality for the decoding operation:

The circuit should decode the encoded data values and output the original data values.
To implement the run-length decoding, you should use Verilog code to read the encoded data values and output the original data values based on the count of each encoded data value.
